text:
Maya: Deploybot flagged a regression during the canary for v3.5.0-rc2 — p95 on /generate jumped ~3% around 10:18 UTC. Deploybot suggested hold, autopilot is suppressed for this release. Can we decide: pause rollforward and run manual probes?
Ben: Confirming. Spike started 10:18–10:20, host-05 mem climbed ~12%. No errors yet, just latency.
Priya: +1 to pause. I'll run targeted probe against the canary group and compare traces.
deploybot: ALERT: canary latency threshold breached (p95 > 2.2s). Suggested action: hold traffic, run canary-probe, and surface traces.
Maya: Pausing rollforward now. Executed: `/deploy pause v3.5.0-rc2 --scope=canary` (manual).
Maya: Starting manual probe — running health + synthetic generation.
Priya: probe results (excerpt):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/run -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq '.latency'
# sample latency series: [0.12,0.13,2.41,2.45,0.14]
```
Priya: Those two 2.4s samples line up with the spike window. I'm pulling traces now.
Ben: Traces show increased KV cache misses on canary instances. Noticed a kernel flag changed in rc2 that touches prefetched KV behavior.
Jorge: Heads up — Dedicated customers are pinned to v3.4.8. If we need to roll back the hosted canary, we should avoid touching dedicated pools. I'll standby for pin requests.
Maya: Rollback criteria proposal: auto/manual decision matrix — if p95 > 2.5s for 5m OR error rate > 1% for 3m => execute manual rollback to v3.4.8 (canary first, then staged). Otherwise keep paused and run deeper probes for 30m. Thoughts?
Ben: Agree with criteria. Add: if KV-miss rate correlates with latency in traces -> rollback ASAP. Also note cache flush may be required after rollback.
Priya: I'll run an A/B synthetic that isolates KV calls vs token gen to validate root cause. ETA 12m.
Sam: Support & comms: Preparing customer note draft (internal): "We paused the staged rollout of v3.5.0-rc2 due to a latency regression in canary; investigating. No customer-facing impact observed on dedicated pools. We'll update in 30 minutes."
Maya: Release notes PR #1234 mentions "KV cache prefetch optimization" — that aligns with Ben's observation. If rollback needed, we should revert that change in the release branch and include a note about cache behavior.
Jorge: If we roll back, I'll coordinate pin for Dedicated only if customers ask. Default is to keep dedicated pinned to 3.4.8.
Maya: Rollback playbook (brief):
1) Execute `/deploy rollback canary v3.4.8 --wait=10m`
2) Monitor p50/p95/error for 15m, check traces for KV misses
3) If stable, stage 20% traffic -> 100% over 30m with guard rails
4) Publish rollback notes and update PR reverting the KV change
(Also: ensure tf/cache flush command: `svc cache flush --scope=canary` after rollback if needed)
Priya: Probe complete: latency correlation to KV misses confirmed on canary trace samples.
Maya: OK taking action. Ben, Jorge, please be ready to run rollback when I say go. Sam, prep the external churn-free note: short + non-alarming.
Ben: Ready. I'll have the rollback script open and confirm preflight checks.
Jorge: Ready to lock dedicated pools if support flags any customer impact.
Sam: Draft ready, ping me when rollback in progress so I can push notice to internal-status and update the customer doc.
ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-7890 for this pause/investigation: https://incidents.redwood/INC-7890
Maya: Rolling back canary to v3.4.8 in 3...2...1. `/deploy rollback canary v3.4.8`
deploybot: ROLLBACK STARTED: canary -> v3.4.8. Watch p95 and error-rate dashboards.
Ben: Rollback completed on canary, running validation checks.
Priya: Validation pass: p95 returned to baseline, KV-miss rate back down. Traces look clean.
Maya: Staging traffic to 20% now, monitor 30m then proceed.
Sam: Internal status updated + customer-facing blurb queued.
Jorge: No dedicated customer reports. Leaving pins as-is.
Maya: Postmortem to follow — initial hypothesis: KV prefetch optimization caused regressions at certain sequence lengths under batch patterns. Will open a revert PR and include test harness for KV perf.
Ben: Thanks everyone. Good fast follow. :thumbsup:
Priya: Filed trace snippets and probe logs in ticket INC-7890.
Maya: Closing thread for now — will reopen if anything new pops.
